title: The dynamical environment of the high-mass star-forming region G28.288-0.364
question: What are the physical and kinematic properties and evolutionary stages of the embedded H II regions and surrounding dense dust cores in the massive star-forming region G28.288–0.364?

what.value: Near kinematic distance of 3.3 kpc and systemic velocity of 48.7 km s^-1

evidence.quote: (cite: 2012ApJ...756...60S) have reported a systemic velocity of 48.7 km s$^{-1}$ for G28.288–0.364. They have also put this star-forming region at a near kinematic distance of 3.3 kpc, which is also consistent with the distance estimations of (cite: 2006ApJ...653.1325S) and (cite: 2016ApJ...823...77R).

what.value: THOR 1.44 GHz, CORNISH 4.86 GHz, GLOSTAR-D 5.79 GHz, and GLOSTAR-D+Effelsberg 5.85 GHz radio continuum flux densities

what.value: Dust temperature T_d = 30.9 K for the parent ATLASGAL clump

evidence.quote: and $T_{\rm d}$ = 30.9 K for the entire ATLASGAL clump (cite: 2022MNRAS.510.3389U).

what.value: Dust opacity κ_ν0 = 0.899 cm^2 g^-1 at 1.3 mm for MRN grain distribution with thin ice mantles, and dust emissivity index β = 2.0

evidence.quote: where $\beta$ is the dust emissivity index, adopted as 2.0 (cite: 2013A&A...554A..42R) in our calculations.

evidence.quote: Applying this procedure to the extracted molecular line spectra, (cite: 2018ApJS..235....3Y) derived the velocity intervals corresponding to the blue- and redshifted outflow lobes of the parent ATLASGAL clump and estimated a mass entrainment rate of 26.60$\times$10$^{-4}$ M$_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$.

recipe.goal: Measure multi-frequency radio continuum flux densities, spectral index, and deconvolved H II region sizes
recipe.method: Measure integrated radio continuum flux densities above a 3σ threshold from 1.35 to 5.85 GHz maps to fit a power-law spectral index (S_ν ∝ ν^α), and fit 2D Gaussians to the 5 GHz CORNISH components (CORNISH-A and CORNISH-B) using CASA imfit.

recipe.goal: Extract and fit radio recombination line (RRL) spectra from GLOSTAR-D and ALMA Band 3
recipe.method: Extract average RRL spectrum from a one-beam circular region in GLOSTAR-D, and extract individual H63δ spectra toward CORNISH-A and CORNISH-B from the ~1'' ALMA Band 3 cube, fitting Gaussian profiles to obtain central velocities and FWHMs.
key_parameters: Circular extraction aperture of diameter = 1 synthesized beam (25'') for GLOSTAR-D
assumptions: Classification thresholds of Kurtz (2005), Sewilo et al. (2004), Keto et al. (2008): HC H II regions have sizes <= 0.03 pc and RRL FWHM >= 40 km s^-1; UC H II regions have sizes <= 0.1 pc and RRL FWHM ~ 30 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Identify compact 1.36 mm dust cores and measure their sizes and flux densities
recipe.method: Run dendrogram analysis with astrodendro on the ALMAGAL 1.36 mm dust continuum map to identify candidate core leaves, then fit 2D Gaussians with CASA imfit using dendrogram leaf parameters as initial guesses and bounding boxes.
key_parameters: min_value = 3σ, min_delta = 1σ, min_npix = 1 synthesized beam area
Post-fit filtering: F_peak > 5σ and aspect ratio <= 3

recipe.goal: Derive isothermal core masses, surface densities, number densities, and correct for free-free contamination
recipe.method: Calculate isothermal dust masses, surface densities, and number densities from 1.36 mm integrated fluxes using Eqs. (1)–(3). For cores with CORNISH 5 GHz counterparts (MM3 and MM4), extrapolate the 5 GHz flux density to 220.6 GHz assuming optically thin free-free emission (α = -0.1) and subtract it before recomputing dust masses.
assumptions: Optically thin dust emission; gas-to-dust ratio δ_gd = 100; dust opacity κ_ν0 = 0.899 cm^2 g^-1 at 1.3 mm with β = 2.0; dust temperature T_d = 30.9 K; distance D = 3.3 kpc; mean molecular weight μ ≈ 2.8
Optically thin free-free spectral index α = -0.1 above the 5 GHz CORNISH frequency for MM3 and MM4; zero free-free contamination for MM1, MM2, MM5

recipe.goal: Identify molecular transitions and model LTE rotational temperatures and column densities toward the five dust cores
recipe.method: Identify molecular lines in ALMAGAL Band 6 cubes using CASSIS with CDMS and JPL catalogs, then fit 1D LTE radiative transfer models using XCLASS to derive rotational temperatures (from H2CO transitions) and column densities for DCN, H2CO, HC3N, C18O, 13CO, and SO, plus construct a DCN (3–2) moment 0 map.
key_parameters: Free parameters per component: source size (θ_source), rotational temperature (T_rot), column density (N), linewidth (Δv), velocity offset (v_off)
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), justified by core number densities n >= 10^6 cm^-3, and T_kin ≈ T_rot
